Gaza · October 2023 to September 2026

Seeing is believing.

First, Gaza from space, before and now. Then ten numbers, each given the whole screen. If it becomes too much, the button at the bottom takes you straight to the companies that supplied it.

Scroll to begin

The war began after the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, which killed over 1,200 people and took 251 hostage. A ceasefire began on 10 October 2025; people are still being killed under it. Every number names who counted it: UN United Nations · Ref Western reference statistics · Gaza Gaza authorities, as published by the UN · Israel Israel's own figures.

11 · Who supplied it

These companies made the machines. What you do about it is your choice.

Each is documented as supplying products or services used in the war on Gaza, a war the UN Commission of Inquiry concluded amounts to genocide. Each card shows who owns the company, which funds have already walked away, and a link to the company’s own contact page.

United States · Heavy equipment

CATERPILLAR

The D9 bulldozer: 50 tonnes, plus about 8 tonnes of armour for the Israeli army. Human rights groups have documented armoured D9s levelling homes, shelters and farmland across Gaza.

$295MD9 sale approved by the US government, 28 Feb 2025
WaivedCongressional review, after an emergency was declared

12 · Your choice

What you do now is your choice.

No one can make it for you. But every pension, savings fund and purchase is already a choice, and most of us make it without looking. Now you have looked.

“…silence would have made me feel guilty of complicity.”

Albert Einstein, 1954
  1. Decide where you stand.Read the evidence, the record and what Israel and the companies say in reply, then make up your own mind. This page gives the facts. The judgement is yours.
  2. Find out what your money supports.Pensions, KiwiSaver, superannuation, 401(k)s and index funds often hold the companies above. Most providers publish their full list of holdings. If yours doesn’t, ask.
  3. Move it, if you choose to.You can switch to a fund that excludes weapons makers or the companies you object to, or ask your broker or adviser what your options are. Some of the world’s largest funds have already made that choice: see Divested on the cards above.
  4. Tell the companies, in your own words.Each card links to the company’s own contact page. Say what you think and why, calmly and factually. A message in your own words carries more weight than a template.
  5. Tell the people around you.Talk to friends, family and colleagues, and to whoever runs your workplace pension. Share this page so they can see the evidence for themselves.
Questions you can ask your pension provider or broker
  • Does my fund hold shares or bonds in any of the companies listed on this page?
  • What is your policy on investing in companies whose products are used in armed conflicts?
  • Do you offer an option that excludes these companies, and how would I switch to it?

This page is information, not financial or legal advice. Before moving investments, check fees, tax and timing with your provider or a licensed adviser.

13 · The record

What the courts and the UN have said.

  • Sep 2025The UN Commission of Inquiry concludes Israel's conduct in Gaza amounts to genocide.
  • Dec 2024Amnesty International concludes Israel committed genocide. Human Rights Watch documents extermination and starvation.
  • 21 Nov 2024The International Criminal Court issues arrest warrants for Benjamin Netanyahu and Yoav Gallant, and for a Hamas commander.
  • 26 Jan 2024The International Court of Justice orders Israel to prevent genocidal acts and let aid in. The case continues.
What Israel says

Israel rejects these findings. It says it acted in self-defence after 7 October and that Hamas fights from civilian areas. No court has given a final ruling.
